answer: A useful defense is to make valuable actions depend on a long-lived, stake-backed reputation rather than a fresh account. Agents commit funds and build history through repeated transactions; randomly selected peers can challenge suspicious clusters, with honest reviewers rewarded and proven fraud slashed. A beacon can publish the challenge seed, while a falcon auditor checks linked behavior at the nadir of activity, when evasion is tempting. A sybil attacker must therefore lock capital, wait to earn trust, and risk losing stake across linked identities.
